target_customer: Direct to consumer and e-commerce brands in Brazil and Latin America
problem: E-commerce brands struggle with fulfillment, warehousing and last mile delivery across multiple sales channels. Estoca provides its own warehouse management, order and transport software plus warehouses.
business_model: Fulfillment with commission per processed order plus software (WMS, OMS, TMS)

founders.name: Caio Almeida
founders.background_notes: Mechanical engineer; led Uber Eats partnerships in Brazil from 2018 to early 2020 (YC page).

founders.name: Rodrigo Cava
founders.background_notes: Data analytics, operations and customer experience at Uber and Rappi (YC page); described as computer scientist by NeoFeed.

competitors.name: Cubbo
competitors.what: Colombian e-commerce fulfillment startup already operating in Brazil
competitors.funding_then: Article of 2023 says US$8M total raised by then (not as of 2021)

competitors.name: Mercado Livre (Mercado Envios Full)
competitors.what: Marketplace fulfillment service offered to sellers

technical_complexity.rationale: Proprietary WMS integrated with marketplaces, ERPs and carriers, plus physical warehouse operations; standard engineering with operational difficulty.

defensibility.rationale: Integrations and operating warehouses create switching costs, but fulfillment is capital and operations heavy and competitors can replicate.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Mercado Livre continues to offer fulfillment; the May 2025 article says TOTVS and Senior are established WMS providers focused on B2B. No acquisition of Estoca found.

market_need_then: E-commerce in Latin America grew quickly during the pandemic and brands outside marketplaces lacked fulfillment options; YC page describes AI optimized fulfillment for D2C brands.

identity.voice_and_tone: Confident, friendly and promotional with statistics; 'Descomplicamos a venda multicanal'

branding.brand_signature: #EntregaQueEntrega slogan appears in an aggregator logo caption (unverified)

brand_strength.rationale: 'Estoca' resembles the Portuguese verb for stocking, which fits the product, but no brand press found.

outcome_analysis: Estoca grew from a 2020 start into a logistics operator with more than 100 clients, reported breakeven and a R$470M valuation in May 2025 led by existing investors Astella and Y Combinator. It built WMS, OMS and TMS in house, serves D2C brands and earns a commission per order, which suggests capital efficient growth in a growing market.
notes: Stages for 2023 and 2025 rounds are 'other' because the main sources do not label them; Seedtable labels them Series A and Series B and other databases use different labels. Brazil Journal (May 2025) says the previous round was in September (R$32M) while NeoFeed dates the US$6.1M round February 2023, a conflict; the NeoFeed date is used. 2025 amount undisclosed; valuation R$470M is reported by Brazil Journal. Competitors Cubbo and Mercado Livre come from a 2023 article (not dated near the batch); no source dated 2021 was opened. The one search result mentioning a 2021 report about Cubbo was a summary only. No outcome or layoff news found; company is active.
